// P-FLOW-08 / P-200 RED fixture for `flow-determinism` (contract 1.6 / index 9.2, architecture
// §10.3) — the lint MUST reject this. A `myelin-flow` workflow BODY (`// @workflow-body`) that
// reads the wall clock, a real RNG, and sleeps via raw `std`/`tokio` calls INSTEAD of the
// deterministic `WfCtx` surface. Each raw non-deterministic read makes replay diverge: on
// re-execution from the journal the workflow would draw a DIFFERENT time / random number, so the
// command sequence no longer matches the journal — the non-deterministic-replay bug class (the
// divergence guard P-FLOW-07 halts such a run as nondeterministic + dead-letters it; this lint
// stops the body from compiling in the first place).
//
// NOT real crate code — it lives under `/fixtures/` (excluded from the live workspace lint-gate)
// and is scanner DATA for the committed-ratchet self-test (`tests/lint_fixtures.rs`). The GREEN
// fixture (`flow_determinism.flow.green.rs.txt`) expresses the SAME logic through `ctx.now()` /
// `ctx.rand()` / `ctx.activity(..)` and IS real code that compiles against the real `WfCtx`.
use std::time::SystemTime;

// @workflow-body — this fn is a durable workflow body; the flow-determinism lint fires here.
pub fn nightly_digest_workflow(ctx: &mut WfCtx) {
    // RED: raw wall-clock read — replay would return a DIFFERENT instant (must go through ctx.now()).
    let started_at = SystemTime::now();
    // RED: a real RNG draw — replay would draw a DIFFERENT number (must go through ctx.rand()).
    let jitter = rand::random::<u64>();
    let _shard = jitter % 16;
    // RED: a raw timer sleep — a workflow must park durably via ctx.sleep_for(), not block a worker.
    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30));
    // RED: a raw v4 UUID — non-deterministic entropy; an id a workflow needs must be journaled.
    let _id = Uuid::new_v4();
    let _ = (started_at, ctx);
}
